newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BOLIVIAN VICE PRESIDENT APPEALS FOR LOWER TICKET PRICES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLIVIAN VICE PRESIDENT APPEALS FOR LOWER TICKET PRICES.

text.p: The Vice President of Bolivia, the nation hosting the Copa America soccer tournament which has been hit by poor attendance, appealed Monday for organisers to reduce the price of tickets for games.
Victor Hugo Cardenas made his request following numerous matches in recent days played in near empty stadiums. Even the hosts themselves have played to shockingly small crowds.
Cardenas said he made in the request in a letter to Romero Osuna, president of the tournament's organising committee.
"I sent .. a letter expressing my deep concern at the high ticket prices for the games at this Copa America, which are keeping the public away from the games.
"The prices are really prohibative," said Cardenas, who added that he is a soccer fanatic who never misses an international game in La Paz.
"We want the Bolivian people to accompany not just the Bolivian team but all the teams in large numbers."
Prices vary between $6 and $30, considered extremly high in a country where the average annual per capita income is $800.
The tournament has also been devalued because it clashes with the region's South American World Cup qualifying matches, causing many teams to bring reserve sides.
Only the group C games in Santa Cruz have so far attracted anything like a full house.
Just 15,000 people watched Bolivia beat Peru 2-0 Sunday in the 45,000 capacity Hernando Silas stadium, while a mere 2,000 attended Peru's win over Uruguay.
